proposals.relationship: Black challenges the modernisation-as-secularisation premise he attributes jointly to Durkheim and Weber, arguing that its secular concept of reason obscures past military cultures.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2020 chapter27 explicitly names both sociologists before criticizing the premise’s circularity, selective evidence and failure to understand past military values. This is Black’s bounded collective attribution and critique; his preceding26distinction between Durkheimian constraints and Weberian contingent outcomes is retained. Neither sociologist’s original texts were collated; no claim that their complete theories are identical, that either personally influenced Black, or that every military-revolution proponent follows them.

proposals.relationship: Responding to Janowski’s Marx/Mill comparison, Black rejects deterministic historical teleology as empirically and morally flawed because it effaces complexity, free will and moral choice.
proposals.evidence_note: Own final2020interview answer138addresses Janowski’s explicitly repeated Marx/Mill interpretation, following the quoted comparison134–135. This is an interviewer-framed critique of a particular attributed vision, not an independent collation of Marx’s writings or a claim that every Marxian account is identical. The interviewer’s quotation is attributed to Marx without edition/coauthor detail; Marx/Engels originals were not collated and sole authorship is not asserted. Mill co-subject retained, exact endpoint absent. Black’s broader political claims remain his2020testimony, not certified current facts.
